verified_ok: (1) CVT/width rule (RISCVInstrInfo.cpp isFrepSequenced, 32cfaf98fa8c). An opcode whose name contains 'CVT' answers no, and so does an instruction with FP register operands of different widths. Independent completeness check: I extracted the 'nseq' mnemonics from GVSoC isa_riscv_gen.py and isa_smallfloats.py (165 by my parse, comment lines excluded; the worker counts 159) and matched them against llvm-tblgen -dump-json of wt/20-F014's RISCV.td. 121 map to LLVM instruction AsmStrings and 55 to InstAliases (the .ah forms and fmv.x.s/fmv.s.x). Every target instruction has CVT in its name, a GPR operand, or mixed FP widths, so isFrepSequenced answers no for every nseq instruction: 0 overcounts. The mnemonics missing from LLVM (.ah forms, vfeq.r.ah etc.) either are aliases covered above or have no LLVM instruction. Safety direction: the rule can only remove instructions from the counted set, for example sequenced mixed-width Xsmallfloat ops such as vfcpka.h.s or fmacex, or any sequenced opcode with CVT in its name. Removing an instruction makes the walk reach its Nth counted instruction later, so the protected range only grows, which costs performance and is never a miscompile. Counted FP loads/stores keep their GPR address allowance (FLD/FSD/FLW/FSW/FLH/FSH), consistent with the GVSoC fp_op tags.

(2) logs/20-F014/rev3/fcvth.ll: int-20 at -O2 (default and -enable-post-misched) puts the unrelated 'fsh fa2, %lo(gh)' right after fdiv.d, and -misched=ilpmin reorders the body. 20-F014 keeps 'fdiv.d; fadd.d; fcvt.s.d; fcvt.h.s; fadd.h' in pass order under default, -enable-post-misched, -misched=ilpmin and -misched=ilpmax. The pass's N=5 there still counts the two conversions, which is the pre-existing SNITCHFrepLoops defect the note reports, not this change. [fa, fcvt.h.s, fb] with N=2 is correct by construction: FCVT_H_S has 'CVT' in its name, so it is not counted, fb gets count 2 <= 2, and fb is a boundary. The pass cannot currently emit N=2 for such a body, because of that same defect.
